The point is that the officers can NEVER really know what is in a vehicle until they get there and look inside, which, by that time, can be too late.

Here's my viewpoint as a Brit. Most of the population in the UK do not own a firearm. To the general populace, a gun is something seen on TV, on movies, or - very rarely - in the hands of dedicated firearms police officers. The majority of our police force are equally unarmed, save for batons, pepper spray and tasers (which are questionable, but a different matter than firearms.)

Without this culture of guns = order, the police are immediately more approachable. It is very unlikely a police officer can kill you within a few seconds, even if he or she wanted to. The police aren't necessarily something to be feared, because they aren't carrying something inherently dangerous.
